id: When I Heard at the Close of the Day

prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

When I heard at the close of the day how my name had been receiv’d with plaudits in the capitol, still it was not a happy night for me that follow’d, And else when I carous’d, or when my plans were accomplish’d, still I was not happy, But the day when I rose at dawn from the bed of perfect health, refresh’d, singing, inhaling the ripe breath of autumn, When I saw the full moon in the west grow pale and disappear in the morning light, When I wander’d alone over the beach, and undressing bathed, laughing with the cool waters, and saw the sun rise, And when I thought how my dear friend my lover was on his way coming, O then I was happy, O then each breath tasted sweeter, and all that day my food nourish’d me more, and the beautiful day pass’d well, And the next came with equal joy, and with the next at evening came my friend, And that night while all was still I heard the waters roll slowly continually up the shores, I heard the hissing rustle of the liquid and sands as directed to me whispering to congratulate me, For the one I love most lay sleeping by me under the same cover in the cool night, In the stillness in the autumn moonbeams his face was inclined toward me, And his arm lay lightly around my breast – and that night I was happy.

prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: When, And, But

outputs.L1:
When, at the close of day, I heard how my name had been received with plaudits in the Capitol, the night that followed was still not a happy one for me. Nor was I happy when I caroused or when my plans were accomplished.  

But on the day when I rose at dawn from the bed of perfect health—refreshed and singing, inhaling the ripe breath of autumn—when I saw the full moon in the west grow pale and disappear into the morning light; when I wandered alone along the beach and, undressing, bathed, laughing in the cool waters, and watched the sun rise; and when I thought of how my dear friend, my lover, was on his way to me—oh, then I was happy.  

Then each breath tasted sweeter, my food nourished me more fully, and the beautiful day passed well. The next day came with equal joy, and on the following evening my friend arrived.  

That night, while all was still, I heard the waters rolling slowly and continually upon the shore. I heard the hissing rustle of water and sand, as though whispering directly to me in congratulation. For the one I loved most lay sleeping beside me, beneath the same cover in the cool night. In the stillness, amid the autumn moonbeams, his face was inclined toward mine, and his arm rested lightly across my breast—and that night, I was happy.
outputs.L2:
At day’s end, I learned that my name had been greeted with applause in the capital, yet the night that followed brought me no joy. Nor was I truly content when I drank and celebrated, or when my ambitions succeeded.  

But one autumn morning, I awoke at sunrise in flawless health, restored and singing, drawing in the rich air of the season. I watched the full moon fade in the western sky until it vanished into daylight. Alone, I roamed the shore, removed my clothes, and plunged laughing into the cool water as the sun appeared. Then I remembered that my beloved friend was traveling toward me, and happiness filled me. Every breath seemed sweeter, my meals sustained me more deeply, and the lovely hours passed in contentment.  

The following day was equally joyful, and by the next evening my friend had arrived. That night, in the surrounding silence, I listened to the waves moving slowly and endlessly onto the beach. The soft hiss of water against sand seemed like a private whisper offering congratulations. Beneath the same covering, in the cool night, the person I loved above all others slept beside me. In the quiet autumn moonlight, his face turned toward mine, his arm resting gently across my chest—and that night, I knew happiness.
outputs.L3:
Public acclaim, joyful celebrations, and the fulfillment of long-held ambitions did not bring the speaker genuine happiness. Instead, true contentment arose from simple, intimate experiences. The speaker discovered joy in waking healthy and refreshed on a beautiful autumn morning, fully alive to the promise of the day.

This happiness deepened through solitary encounters with nature: watching the moon slowly fade, bathing in the cool water, and witnessing the sun rise. Such quiet moments created a powerful sense of peace and connection with the natural world. The anticipation of a beloved friend’s arrival made life even sweeter, enriching every breath, every meal, and every passing day.

Yet the speaker’s greatest happiness came through closeness with the beloved. Lying together at night, held in a silent embrace while the waters rolled gently along the shore, offered a fulfillment that fame and achievement could never provide. Ultimately, the speaker finds lasting joy not in public success, but in health, nature, anticipation, intimacy, and love.
outputs.L4:
The speaker begins by reflecting on the rewards that people commonly associate with happiness: public praise, lively celebration, and the satisfaction of seeing long-held ambitions fulfilled. Yet each of these pleasures proves strangely hollow. Acclaim fades almost as soon as it is received, revelry leaves behind exhaustion and silence, and even success cannot provide lasting contentment. The very things that once seemed desirable lose their power when they are finally attained.

Against these empty triumphs, the speaker considers quieter and more enduring sources of joy. Good health allows a person to experience the world fully, while nature offers beauty, peace, and renewal without demanding recognition in return. Anticipation can be sweeter than possession, because hope keeps desire alive in a way that achievement often cannot. These reflections gradually turn away from outward accomplishment and toward the private life of feeling.

The speaker ultimately discovers that his deepest happiness lies in intimate companionship. In the calm presence of his beloved, he no longer needs applause, excitement, or proof of success. Shared silence, affection, and physical closeness provide a sense of fulfillment that public honors cannot match. Love nourishes him because it is personal, mutual, and immediate. The passage therefore suggests that true happiness is found not in status or achievement, but in the quiet comfort of being close to someone who is deeply loved.
outputs.L5:
**When, And, But**

*When*, *and*, and *but* are small words that help connect ideas.

**When** refers to time:  
*When the sun rises, the city wakes up.*

**And** joins related ideas:  
*People open their windows, and birds begin to sing.*

**But** introduces a contrast:  
*The morning is beautiful, but it does not last forever.*

Together, these words make writing clearer and more expressive:  
*When a new day begins, we make plans and follow our hopes, but we must also be ready for unexpected changes.*

### “When I Heard at the Close of the Day”  
*Walt Whitman*

When I heard at the close of the day how my name had been receiv’d with plaudits in the capitol, still it was not a happy night for me that follow’d,  
And else when I carous’d, or when my plans were accomplish’d, still I was not happy,  
But the day when I rose at dawn from the bed of perfect health, refresh’d, singing, inhaling the ripe breath of autumn,  
When I saw the full moon in the west grow pale and disappear in the morning light,  
When I wander’d alone over the beach, and undressing bathed, laughing with the cool waters, and saw the sun rise,  
And when I thought how my dear friend my lover was on his way coming, O then I was happy,  
O then each breath tasted sweeter, and all that day my food nourish’d me more, and the beautiful day pass’d well,  
And the next came with equal joy, and with the next at evening came my friend,  
And that night while all was still I heard the waters roll slowly continually up the shores,  
I heard the hissing rustle of the liquid and sands as directed to me whispering to congratulate me,  
For the one I love most lay sleeping by me under the same cover in the cool night,  
In the stillness in the autumn moonbeams his face was inclined toward me,  
And his arm lay lightly around my breast—and that night I was happy.
